sections.title: 56.1 Tail-latency amplification
sections.body:
If an orchestrator launches 20 independent workers and each has a 1% probability of missing its latency target:

\[
P(at\ least\ one\ slow)
=1-0.99^{20}
\approx18.21\%
\]

This assumes the parent waits for all workers.

Parallel execution can improve median latency while making tail latency worse.

steps.narration: A coordinator decomposes work and assigns ownership to specialists.

steps.label: Delegate
steps.narration: Tasks are handed off with clear inputs, outputs, and termination conditions.

steps.label: Specialists
steps.narration: Specialist agents execute narrow skills and return structured results.

sections.title: 56.3 Speculative execution
sections.body:
An application might anticipate that an agent will require an authorized customer-order lookup and begin that read while the model classifies the query.

If the prediction is correct, latency decreases.

If incorrect, resources have been wasted.

A simplified expected latency benefit is:

\[
Benefit=pS-(1-p)H
\]

Where \(p\) is prediction accuracy, \(S\) is expected time saved and \(H\) is additional latency overhead from incorrect speculation.

Cost must be assessed separately.

Speculative execution should be limited to appropriately authorized, low-risk operations. Never speculatively execute irreversible transactions.

steps.label: Goal
steps.narration: The agent receives a user goal and must decide what information or tools are required.

steps.label: Reason
steps.narration: The model plans the next action instead of answering blindly.

steps.label: Act / tool
steps.narration: The agent calls an authorized tool or function with structured arguments. Never speculatively execute irreversible transactions.

steps.label: Observe
steps.narration: Usage, cost, latency, and traces are recorded for FinOps and incident response.

steps.label: Decide
steps.narration: The loop continues, escalates to a human, or finishes with a grounded answer.

sections.title: 56.4 Early stopping and quorum
sections.body:
Some research tasks can finish after enough independent evidence has been obtained.

However, a procurement approval requiring all mandatory checks cannot use a majority quorum to ignore a failed compliance check.

The stopping policy must depend on which requirements are optional and which are mandatory.
